title: Ruskatux (Seaman's Neck)
summary: A Seaford / Seaman's Neck placename for meadows and uplands east of an earlier Indian purchase.
introduction_content: Ruskatux is recorded as a neck of land at Seaford, sometimes known as Seaman's Neck.
history_content: Ruskatux covered more than 1,500 acres of meadows and uplands east of an earlier Indian purchase and the Governor Kieft patent. English records also associate the place with Seaman's Neck, named for Captain John Seaman.
translation_content:
Ruskatux is related to Algonquian words for rushes, meadow, grass, or hay land, and interpreted as a place of rushes, meadow, or grass land.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names can encapsulate local knowledge, reference local biocultural heritage, signify past and present biodiversity, and showcase local and Indigenous populations’ perceptions of and interactions with natural environments.”

— Maria Fedina, Indigenous presence and belonging in urban areas: the case of the urban Komi homemaking and place-naming (2025), section: The power of place names: asserting presence and preserving ancestral knowledge
preservation_content: Ruskatux keeps an older Native place-name attached to the marsh and neck landscape of Seaford. The name helps connect today's south-shore neighborhoods with the meadow geography that shaped Native and colonial land records.
